subject: Miranda Briseño City Council Candidacy
overview: Candidate Miranda Briseño discussed her background in urban planning and her platform emphasizing sidewalk accessibility, public seating, and inclusive municipal services.

items.title: Introduction and Professional Background
items.summary: Miranda Briseño introduced herself as a Hillside resident and MassDOT planner with a background in urban planning and pedestrian advocacy.

items.title: Candidacy and Community Involvement
items.summary: Briseño detailed her path to running for City Council, citing her experience at Medford City Hall and her involvement with Our Revolution Medford and local mutual aid.

items.title: Accessibility and Infrastructure
items.summary: The candidate prioritized physical accessibility improvements, including sidewalk repairs, curb ramps, and the completion of a citywide ADA transition plan.

items.title: Public Seating and Hostile Architecture
items.summary: Briseño advocated for increasing public seating and removing 'hostile architecture' elements, such as armrests on benches, to better support all residents and travelers.

items.title: Housing and Social Policy
items.summary: The discussion covered Briseño's support for harm reduction policies and the removal of barriers to housing and basic services for unhoused populations.
